Add GPS coordinates to the plots of a design

Source: R/plot_coordinates.R
add_plot_coordinates.Rd

Adds the GPS position of every plot to design$design, so that save_breedbase() saves it with the plots and Breedbase shows the trial on its field map. Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees (as from a phone or GPS). There are three ways to give them:

Usage

add_plot_coordinates(
  design,
  coordinates = NULL,
  latitude = NULL,
  longitude = NULL,
  origin = NULL,
  plot_width = NULL,
  plot_length = NULL,
  col_gap = 0,
  row_gap = 0,
  col_bearing = 90,
  row_bearing = 0
)

Arguments

design

A design from augmented_row_column_design(), augmented_prep_design(), resolvable_row_column_design(), as_breedbase_design() or prepare_breedbase_trial().

coordinates

Optional table of coordinates, as described above.

latitude, longitude

Optional point per plot, as described above.

origin

Optional c(latitude, longitude) of the outer corner of the plot in row 1, column 1. For a p-rep design with several locations, a list with one such pair per location, named by location.

plot_width, plot_length

Plot size in metres: plot_width across columns (from column 1 towards column 2), plot_length across rows (from row 1 towards row 2). Used with origin.

col_gap, row_gap

Space in metres between plots of neighbouring columns and rows (alleys). Used with origin.

col_bearing, row_bearing

Compass direction (degrees clockwise from north) in which column numbers and row numbers increase; they must be at right angles. The default puts column 1 at the west, columns running east, and row 1 at the south, rows running north. Used with origin.

Value

The design with the coordinate columns added.

Details

  • From the field corner (origin): give the GPS of the outer corner of the plot in row 1, column 1, the plot size and the directions in which rows and columns run. The four corners of every plot are calculated from its row and column.

  • One point per plot (latitude, longitude): vectors with one value per row of design$design, or the names of columns of the design that hold them.

  • A table (coordinates), e.g. read with read_breedbase_file(): one row per plot, matched by plot_name (when both have it) or by plot number (plots, plot_number or plot; for p-rep designs also location). It holds either latitude and longitude (or WGS84_x, WGS84_y) for a point, or the eight corner columns of the Breedbase GPS upload template (WGS84_bottom_left_x, WGS84_bottom_left_y, ..., WGS84_top_left_y, where x is the longitude and y the latitude) for a polygon.

With origin, positions are calculated on a local flat approximation of the Earth, accurate to centimetres over a field. The design needs row and col columns (designs converted from agricolae need them in the field book).

The design gets latitude and longitude columns (the centre of the plot), plus the eight corner columns for polygons. They can be edited. save_breedbase() sends a polygon when all eight corner columns of a plot are filled, and otherwise a point from latitude and longitude. Plots without coordinates are saved without them. For a trial that is already in Breedbase, use save_breedbase_coordinates().

Examples

rc <- augmented_row_column_design(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4),
                                  12, 12, 4, 4, n_candidates = 5, seed = 1)
# Plots of 3 m x 5 m, 1 m alleys between rows, columns running east:
rc <- add_plot_coordinates(rc, origin = c(7.4931, 3.9035),
                           plot_width = 3, plot_length = 5, row_gap = 1)
head(rc$design[, c("plots", "row", "col", "latitude", "longitude")])
#>   plots row col latitude longitude
#> 1     1   1   1 7.493123  3.903514
#> 2     2   1   2 7.493123  3.903541
#> 3     3   1   3 7.493123  3.903568
#> 4     4   1   4 7.493123  3.903595
#> 5     5   1   5 7.493123  3.903622
#> 6     6   1   6 7.493123  3.903649

# A field laid out at an angle: columns running north-east.
rc <- add_plot_coordinates(rc, origin = c(7.4931, 3.9035), plot_width = 3,
                           plot_length = 5, col_bearing = 45, row_bearing = 315)

# One GPS point per plot, measured in the field:
pts <- data.frame(plots = rc$design$plots,
                  latitude = 7.4931 + rc$design$row * 5e-5,
                  longitude = 3.9035 + rc$design$col * 3e-5)
rc <- add_plot_coordinates(rc, coordinates = pts)
